calibration.applies: additive offset on the expected ordinal level, selected by the on-device ITA tone band
calibration.note: Bands marked calibrated=false get no offset, so an unmeasured band is never silently corrected.

fallbackHeuristic.note: The ROI heuristic the app ships today, and the thing a trained model has to beat before it may replace it. These are ATTR_THRESHOLDS and ATTR_RAW_KEY in lib/skin.ts, mirrored here so the Python side can score the SAME rule on the SAME validation split without re-deriving it. tests/skin-index-contract.test.ts fails if the two drift. Only the three axes with a scalar ROI feature are listed; the rest have no heuristic to beat, so the gate asks nothing of them.

ordinal.appliesTo: every trained axis, on the overall validation confusion matrix
ordinal.note: Accuracy, ordinal MAE and within-one-grade agreement are all high for a head that always predicts the majority grade, so none of them can tell a learned head from a constant one. Quadratic weighted kappa and the true/predicted correlation both go to 0 for that predictor and are what this floor reads. 0.4 is provisional and was chosen from measured predictors, not from a published benchmark: see docs/ordinal-metric-verification.md.

subgroup.note: A model is promotable only when the worst evaluated subgroup stays within maxAccuracyGap of the mean. A subgroup with too few samples counts as unevaluated, which blocks promotion rather than passing silently. The per-axis qwk/pearson floors are a separate rule and live in promotionGate.ordinal. minQwkGainOverHeuristic is a third, independent rule: the model must BEAT the shipped ROI heuristic in fallbackHeuristic, per axis, on qwk, scored on the same validation rows by the same code (ml/heuristic_baseline.py -> ml/ordinal_metrics.py). The other rules ask whether a model is good; this asks whether it should replace what already ships, which is what the gate is for. 0.0 means strictly greater: a model that merely ties the rule it would replace does not pass. It is 0.0 and not a positive margin because a margin should exceed validation noise and nothing here estimates that noise yet. An axis the heuristic covers but whose ROI feature is missing blocks, and so does a comparison whose two sides were scored on different row counts: you cannot claim to beat a baseline you never scored, or one measured on a different subset.

moisture.head: instrument_only
moisture.why: Corneometer capacitance. An RGB frame does not contain it. ARU may only infer a hydration HINT from visible dryness plus the survey, and must label it as an inference. Supervising a camera head on instrument hydration is allowed only for research on an instrument-paired dataset, never for a product claim.

sensitivity.head: composite
sensitivity.why: Sensitivity is a reaction history, not an appearance. Redness is a symptom, not the axis.
